title: Measuring TCR-pMHC Binding In Situ using a FRET-based Microscopy Assay
protocol: Express B7-1-12H and ICAM-1-12H constructs in high quantities as secreted native proteins using a baculovirus expression system.
Purify the expressed proteins from culture supernatants via Ni-NTA affinity chromatography.
Further purify the proteins through MonoQ anion exchange chromatography.
Proceed with S200 size exclusion chromatography for final purification.
Label one aliquot of purified protein with amine-reactive dyes such as NHS succinimidyl-ester preparations of Alexa Fluor 488 (or FITC), Alexa Fluor 555 (or Cy3), or Alexa Fluor 647 (or Cy5).
Determine the labeling degree of monomeric proteins after S200 size exclusion chromatography by comparing protein absorption at 280 nm and dye absorption at 488 nm, 555 or 552 nm, or 647 nm.
Store unlabeled and fluorophore-labeled proteins at -20°C in PBS plus 50% glycerol.
Refold MHC class II from inclusion bodies expressed in E. coli in the presence of a UV-cleavable peptide substitute for later quantitative exchange with a fluorophore-conjugated peptide of choice.
Purify refolded pMHC complexes by Ni-NTA-affinity chromatography.
Purify refolded pMHC complexes by MonoQ anion-exchange chromatography.
Purify refolded pMHC complexes by S200 gel filtration.
Exchange the UV cleavable peptide with a fluorescent peptide.
Purify monomeric fluorescent pMHC complexes by S200 gel filtration.
Verify quantitative peptide loading by spectrophotometry.
Store proteins at -20°C in PBS/50% glycerol.
Refold scFVs from inclusion bodies expressed in E. coli.
Unfold inclusion bodies in 6 M guanidinium chloride.
Fully reduce unfolded scFVs.
Gradually decrease the concentration of guanidinium chloride to refold scFVs over a week.
Concentrate properly folded scFV using molecular filter units with a cutoff of 10 KDa.
Purify concentrated scFV by S200 gel filtration.
Label monomeric scFV in the presence of 0.05 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP).
Perform labeling reaction at a molar ratio of protein:dye no more than 1:2 at RT for no longer than 2 hours.
Take a fresh vial containing 50 µg fura-2-AM and dissolve it in 50 µl water-free DMSO.
Spin down 106 T-cells for 2 min at 250-400 g.
Resuspend T-cells in 200 µl imaging medium containing Hank's Balanced Salt Solution plus calcium/magnesium and 1% ovalbumin at RT.
Add 1 µl of the fura-2-AM stock solution (1:200 dilution) to the cell suspension, mix well, and incubate at RT for 30 min.
Wash T-cells once in imaging buffer by filling the tube with imaging buffer at RT and pelleting the cells as described.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 200 µl imaging buffer (i.e., at a final density of 5 x 10^6 cells ml^-1).
Place T-cells on a functionalized SLB in imaging buffer (37°C) for calcium measurements or store on ice for up to 3 hr.
Acquire images every 15 to 30 seconds for 30 minutes as soon as T-cells start contacting the SLB.
Excite at 340 +/- 5 nm and detect emission at 510 +/- 40 nm.
Excite at 380 +/- 5 nm and detect emission at 510 +/- 40 nm.
(Note: Respective exposure times depend on the intensity of the excitation light source.)
Add 50-100 μl of pre-warmed anti-pMHC blocking antibody at a final concentration of 20-50 µg/ml after 20-25 minutes into the run.
Continue recording images for another 5 - 10 min to acquire baseline intracellular calcium concentration.
Determine average background fluorescence signal at 340 nm and 380 nm excitation within a region of interest containing no cells.
Background-subtract all measured fura-2 images excited at 340 nm and 380 nm.
Calculate 340 nm/380 nm intensity ratios for individual or group of cells.
Normalize intensity ratios by dividing through the ratio of the five last time frames with complete antibody-blockade of pMHC.
Spin down 10^6 T-cells in a 5 ml polypropylene round-bottom tube for 2 min at 250-400 g.
Decant the media and gently flick the cell pellet.
Add 0.3 μl of scFV (concentration ~ 1 mg/ml) to the cell suspension.
Employ only dye-labeled scFv for bulk FRET measurements.
Incubate the cells on ice for 15 min.
Wash the cells twice through successive centrifugation using ice-cold imaging buffer.
Prepare an SLB containing AF647/Cy5-labeled pMHCs.
Include unlabeled ICAM-1 and B7 in the SLB according to Axmann et al.
Exchange the PBS of the imaging chamber with imaging medium containing Hank's Balanced Salt Solution plus calcium/magnesium and 1% ovalbumin.
Pipette 400 µl of imaging buffer into the well.
Mix carefully.
Remove 400 µl from the well.
Repeat this procedure 3-4 times.
Place the imaging chamber onto the microscope stage.
Adjust the focus until the fluorescent (AF647, Cy5) SLB comes into clear view.
Translate the focused beam parallel to the optical axis to the periphery of the objective’s focal plane via moving of the periscope’s translational stage.
Add T-cells decorated with AF555/Cy3 labeled scFV and let them settle onto the SLB.
Fine-tune the excitation laser beams in TIRF mode until the basal cellular membrane is in focus along with the SLB.
Adjust the laser beam with the periscope’s translational stage if parts of the fluorescent T-cell plasma membrane, which are not in contact with the SLB, appear as a ring.
Use 647 nm excitation at low power to image the FRET acceptor (pMHC) before the bleach pulse.
Use 514 nm excitation at low power to image the FRET donor (TCR) before the bleach pulse.
Use 647 nm excitation at high power to photo-bleach the FRET acceptor.
Use 514 nm excitation at low power to image the FRET donor (TCR) after the bleach pulse.
Use 647 nm excitation at low power to verify complete bleaching of the FRET acceptor.
Select a region of interest (ROI), such as an entire synapse or individual TCR microcluster.
Determine the average intensity in the pre-bleach image (I(3)).
Determine the average intensity in the post-bleach image (I(5)).
Choose a background ROI outside the illumination spot with the same dimensions to determine background intensity (I(background)).
Calculate FRET yield using equation 7.
Perform spatial donor and acceptor channel alignment using multicolored beads that fluoresce in all emission channels.
Determine the spatial shift between both channels due to chromatic aberration by super-positioning individual beads.
Apply the determined spatial correction for one of the two channels for all following 2-color image-pairs.
Determine the degree of donor bleedthrough with an SLB containing only the FRET donor fluorophore.
Alternatively, use FRET-donor-labeled T-cells on a lipid bilayer with unlabeled pMHC to determine bleedthrough.
Determine background outside the illuminated field of view and subtract from both channels.
Calculate the average background-corrected intensities for two corresponding ROIs in the donor channel and acceptor channel.
Calculate the bleedthrough coefficient (BTC) using the formula provided.
Calculate the FRET donor bleedthrough image.
Determine acceptor cross-excitation by exciting an SLB containing the FRET acceptor fluorophore alone with FRET donor excitation light.
Excite the same SLB with acceptor excitation light.
Use background-subtracted images within the FRET acceptor channel to calculate the cross-excitation coefficient (CEC).
Determine the CEC on each measurement day using the laser intensity used for donor excitation.
Calculate the image solely generated through cross-excitation using the resulting CEC.
Calculate the FRET image corrected for bleedthrough and cross-excitation.
Adjust the power of both lasers to give an intensity of 1-5 kW/µm² at the specimen.
Label T-cells with a mix of unlabeled scFV (5-9 parts) and Cy3/AF555-labeled scFV (1 part).
Place an SLB featuring AF647-labeled pMHCs as well as ICAM and B7 on the microscope stage.
Adjust the focus to clearly view the bilayer.
Optional: Insert a slit aperture into the excitation pathway to mask most of the field of illumination except the synapse.
Add H57 scFV decorated T-cells to the bilayer with imaging buffer.
Wait until synapses appear in the field of view.
Take a sequence of 10 to 20 image sets using 2-color detection.
Excite at 514 nm for one color set.
Excite at 647 nm for another color set.
Expose images for 1 to 5 msec and acquire as a set of images.
Apply correction regarding donor bleedthrough and acceptor cross-excitation.
Ensure single molecule FRET events align with single acceptor molecules.
Note the appearance and disappearance of FRET events in one step.
Record traces of single molecule FRET events for several acquisition time frames.
Convert trace lengths into an inverse cumulative decay function.
Normalize the resulting decay function by dividing by the sum of all traces.
Plot normalized values against the number of time frames.
Fit decays with a single exponential function, omitting the last time frame.
Plot the expectation value <n(tlag)> against the delay time tlag using the formula y = 1/exponent.
Fit τoff and <nbleach> based on equation 3 using a non-linear fitting function in a scientific data analysis program.
Calculate the half life of the interaction t1/2 off with t1/2 off = τoff • ln(2).
Determine the conversion factor C for the FRET dye pair using equation 6 and outlined procedures.
Determine the FRET yields for individual TCR microclusters or entire synapses.
Convert all individual FRET yields into TCR occupancies using equation 4.
Convert all TCR occupancies into 2D-KDs using equation 11.
Calculate kon with the law of mass action using kon = koff/KD.
